title: The Lord's Day
definition: The Lord's Day is the first day of the week, associated with Christ's resurrection and the gathered worship of His people.
summary: The Lord's Day is the resurrection-shaped day of Christian worship, remembrance, and gathered devotion to Christ.
christFocus: Jesus Christ rose from the dead and is worshiped by His people as the living Lord.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The Lord's Day is the church's resurrection-centered day of gathered worship and remembrance. Scripture shows the early church gathering on the first day in light of Christ's victory over death.

This doctrine is not mainly about religious rule-keeping or winning calendar debates. It is about a weekly rhythm that reorients believers around the risen Lord, the Word, fellowship, and hope.

Jesus rose on the first day and is the Lord of His people. The Lord's Day reminds the church that Christian life begins from resurrection, not from human striving.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Time easily becomes ruled by work, exhaustion, entertainment, or isolation. The Lord's Day gives believers a repeated invitation to remember who reigns and to gather around Christ's finished and risen life.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Set apart time to worship, rest in Christ, gather with the church as you are able, and re-center your week around the resurrection. Avoid both legalism and neglect.
